introduction: Ford's second-generation GT was developed alongside a Le Mans racer and built around a carbon-fibre tub with a twin-turbo V6. Its narrow teardrop cabin and open flying buttresses channel air through the body, and Ford rated it as its fastest production car at launch.

cutaway.title: Lift the skin off the GT’s V6

chassis.label: Construction
chassis.value: Carbon-fibre monocoque with aluminium front and rear subframes, carbon-fibre body panels

chassis.label: Suspension
chassis.value: Pushrod with hydraulically adjustable ride height

entries.title: Surprise reveal in Detroit
entries.detail: Ford unveiled the new GT at the 2015 North American International Auto Show, presenting a carbon-bodied supercar with an EcoBoost V6 instead of the V8 used by earlier GTs.

entries.title: Class win at Le Mans
entries.detail: The racing version took the GTE-Pro class at the 2016 24 Hours of Le Mans with the No. 68 Ford Chip Ganassi Racing car, fifty years after the GT40's 1966 overall victory.

entries.title: Production begins
entries.detail: Series production of the road car started in December 2016, with first customer cars counted as 2017 models.

sources.title: Ford Authority: The 2017 Ford GT makes 647 horsepower, 216 mph top speed
